## The helpers {#helpers}

The downloadable workspace and the browser lab have the same helpers, with the same names and arguments, and both fit every specification of the menu live. The workspace fits one in well under a second, the browser lab in about a second.

| Helper | Task | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `make_dag(...)`, `plot_dag(dag)` | 2 | Builds the causal graph from arrows written `"cause -> effect"`, one per string, and draws it. |
| `adjustmentSets(dag)` | 2 | Lists what has to be held constant to estimate the effect of concern about immigration on distrust. |
| `paths(dag, Z = ...)` | 2 | Lists every path between concern and distrust, and whether each is open once the comparison holds the variables in `Z` constant. |
| `isAdjustmentSet(dag, ...)` | 2 | Says whether one set of controls, such as the controls of the paper, closes every confounding path without opening another. |
| `fetch_multi100()` | 3 | Workspace only: downloads the file that Multi100 gave the analysts from the OSF, once, into `data_private/`, and checks it. |
| `try_spec(...)` | 4 | Fits one specification and prints the estimate in points of distrust per point of concern with its 95% interval, the *t* test with errors clustered by country, the conventional *t*, the respondents analysed, the partial *r*, the class of the result and its place among the 192 specifications on the curve. |
| `my_experiments()` | 4 | Prints everything that `try_spec()` has fitted so far, side by side, with only the decisions that varied. |
| `submit_exploration()` | 4 | Sends the last `try_spec()` to the class chart as an exploratory result, an open circle, and prints the pre-filled form link and your tag. |
| `my_spec <- prereg()` | 5 | Checks the twelve `my_*` choices of the preregistration block against the menu, prints the block with its estimand statement, and keeps it as `my_spec`. |
| `run_spec(my_spec)` | 5 | Fits the declared specification and prints the same lines as `try_spec()`. It refuses to run if the block has changed since `prereg()`. |
| `report_result()` | 5 | Sends the declared result to the class chart, a filled circle, with the same tag as your exploratory result. |

Both submission functions take `nickname = "..."`, which replaces the tag that they draw for you, such as `amber-otter-42`. Use a nickname rather than your name, because the chart is public.

## The options of each argument {#options}

Every argument of `try_spec()` is one decision of the menu, and the preregistration block of Task 5 names the same decision with `my_` in front (`controls` becomes `my_controls`). The first option of each row is the reference specification, which `try_spec()` fits when it is called with no arguments: 0.1753 points of distrust per point of concern. An option off the curve is refused with the reason why and the page of the course site that teaches it.

| Level | Argument | On the curve | Off the curve |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 – Estimands | `outcome` | `"parliament"`, `"politicians"`, `"legal"`, `"index"` | `"parties"`, `"european_parliament"` |
| | `controls` | `"paper"`, `"none"`, `"demog"`, `"outlook"` | `"paper_no_unhappy"`, `"paper_gov"`, `"paper_macro"` |
| | `weights` | `"none"`, `"design"`, `"population"` | `"post"`, `"post_population"` |
| | `sample` | `"paper"` | `"all_respondents"`, `"all_countries"` |
| 2 – Measurement | `concern` | `"index"` | `"economy"`, `"culture"`, `"place"` |
| | `items` | `"complete"`, `"available"` | – |
| | `education` | `"five"` | `"seven"` |
| | `votes` | `"cabinet"` | `"nonvoters_missing"`, `"largest_party"` |
| | `missing` | `"listwise"` | `"imputation"`, `"as_published"` |
| 3 – Estimation | `fe` | `"country_round"`, `"country_and_round"` | `"random_intercepts"`, `"pooled"` |
| | `errors` | `"country"` | `"country_round"`, `"conventional"`, `"cr2"` |
| | `scale` | `"points"` | `"maximum_effect"`, `"standardised"`, `"r"` |

The five decisions on which the curve keeps more than one option, and what their options mean:

- `outcome` – distrust of the national parliament (`"parliament"`), of politicians (`"politicians"`), of the legal system (`"legal"`), or the mean of the three (`"index"`), each on the trust scale of the ESS turned round, from 0 (complete trust) to 10 (no trust at all).
- `controls` – the individual controls of the paper (`"paper"`); none (`"none"`); age, sex, education and household income (`"demog"`); or those and unhappiness, dissatisfaction with life, rarely meeting friends, interpersonal distrust and left–right position (`"outlook"`). The set of the paper adds the verdicts on the economy, household income, health services and education, and votes for a party in government and for a far-right party.
- `weights` – none (`"none"`); the design weights, which correct for unequal chances of selection (`"design"`); or those times the population weights, so that each country counts by its adult population (`"population"`).
- `items` – a scale (concern, interpersonal distrust, the mean of the trust items) counts only for respondents who answered every one of its items (`"complete"`), or averages the items that they answered (`"available"`).
- `fe` – an intercept for every country-round, so that respondents are compared only with others surveyed in the same country and round (`"country_round"`), or an intercept for every country with a shift for every round (`"country_and_round"`).

The [specification menu](menu.qmd) explains every option, and the [decision map](map.qmd) lays the decisions out in the order in which an analysis meets them.

## Task 3 – the reproduction {#reproduction}

The target is the value that Multi100 recorded for analyst 6U3LL: **t = 46.625** on 72,733 respondents, from the three-level model of Table 3 of the paper without the unemployment rate, fitted with random intercepts for countries and country-rounds.

- **In the workspace**, `fetch_multi100()` downloads the file of the analysts from the OSF (29 MB, once), and the chunk of Task 3 fits the model with `lme4::lmer()`. Run it once at home while online, so that the file is in place on the day. Offline, the report renders everything except this task.
- **In the browser lab**, the file cannot be fetched, because the OSF does not let a page on another website read it. The lab fits the closest specification of the course to the course data instead, `fit_spec(ess, items = "available")`, which gives 0.174.

## Submitting to the chart {#submitting}

You submit twice, and the two submissions are different in kind.

**Task 4 – the exploratory mark (open circle).** Nothing in this task is preregistered.

1. **`try_spec(...)`** – change one argument at a time, for example `try_spec(controls = "none")`. An option off the curve, such as `concern = "culture"`, stops with the reason and the page that teaches it.
2. **`my_experiments()`** – prints everything that you have tried so far.
3. **`submit_exploration()`** – sends the most recent try to the chart. Open the printed link and press **Send**. Note the tag that it prints: it marks your submissions on the class chart.

**Task 5 – the declared mark (filled circle).** Here you preregister one specification before you run it.

4. **Preregister.** Make one choice for every `my_` line of the preregistration block, complete the dotted lines, and run the block, which ends in `my_spec <- prereg()`. The completed block is your preregistration. In the workspace, keep it in the report as set out under [Rendering the report](#rendering-the-report); on the browser lab page, copy the whole cell into your notes.
5. **`run_spec(my_spec)`** – fits your specification and prints its result and its place on the curve.
6. **`report_result()`** – builds your submission from the preregistration and prints a pre-filled form link; open it and press **Send**. It reuses your tag from Task 4. In the browser lab, if you have reloaded the page since then, pass the tag back with `report_result(nickname = "your-tag")`.

If any of that stalls, work down the list under [A stalled browser lab](#a-stalled-browser-lab) in the browser lab, or the [IDE quick fixes](#ide-quick-fixes) in the workspace.

## R idioms for the day {#r-idioms}

- `x <- value` stores a value under a name.
- `source("R/spec_tools.R")` runs a script file; here it loads the helpers.
- `readr::read_csv()`: the part before `::` names the package that the function comes from.
- `ess |> datawizard::data_filter(citizen == 1)` passes the data on to the next step. Read `|>` as 'and then'.
- `datawizard::data_filter()`, `datawizard::data_modify()` and `datawizard::data_summary(..., by = "cntry")` keep some rows, add a column, and summarise by group.
- `datawizard::row_means(d, select = c("a", "b", "c"), min_valid = 3)` averages items across a row, and gives no score to a respondent with fewer than `min_valid` answers.
- `mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)` leaves out missing answers; without `na.rm = TRUE`, a single missing value makes the mean missing.
- `cor(x, y, use = "complete.obs")` is the correlation of two columns, over the rows on which both are answered.
- `performance::cronbachs_alpha(items)` is Cronbach's alpha of a set of items.
- `"parliament"`: options are text, so they go in quotes.
- `# ...`: everything after `#` on a line is a comment, which R ignores. A `#` in front of an arrow of the graph switches it off.
- `lme4::lmer(y ~ x + (1 | cntry), data = d)` fits a multilevel model with a random intercept for each country; `lm(y ~ x + factor(cntry), data = d)` fits the same comparison with fixed effects.
- `?lme4::lmer` opens the help page of a function.
- Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on a Mac) runs the current line, or the selected lines, in the console.
- `quarto preview`, typed in the terminal, renders the report and opens it in a browser.

## A stalled browser lab

The browser lab runs R inside your browser tab, and browsers occasionally baulk. Work down this list. Each step is more certain than the one before, and step 4 puts your mark on the chart whatever your machine does.

1. **Hard reload, then rerun.** Reload the page clearing the cache (Ctrl+Shift+R / Cmd+Shift+R), wait for R and the ESS extract to load again, and **rerun the cells above** the one that failed – the R engine in the browser needs the earlier cells to have run in this session before a later one will work.
2. **Switch browser.** If a cell still will not run, open the browser lab in a different browser (Chrome, Edge or Firefox). A fresh browser clears most stubborn problems.
3. **Follow the shared screen.** If your machine simply will not cooperate, watch the facilitator run the same cell on the shared screen and read the printed results from there. You miss no step by doing this.
4. **Read your printed result to the facilitator.** If `submit_exploration()` or `report_result()` printed your result but the form link will not open, read the printed `b`, `se`, `t`, `df`, `n` and `r` to the facilitator, who adds the mark to the chart for you. If a cell refuses to run at all, nothing is printed and there are no numbers to read, so give the facilitator your five choices instead, and the facilitator reads the result off the curve file by hand (the note below).

::: {.callout-note}
## The by-hand lookup

Last resort, facilitator-side, if the cells of a participant will not run at all: every specification on the curve is one row of `data/spec_curve.csv`, picked by its five codes (`outcome`, `controls`, `weights`, `items`, `fe`), and the reference specification is the row in which `is_reference` is TRUE. Read off `b` and `se` (the form fields `b` and `se`, in points of distrust per point of concern), `stat` (the field `t`, with errors clustered by country), `df` (15), `n` and `r`, and write the label as `explore: [tag] trust outcome=… controls=… weights=… items=… fe=…`, or `declared:` for Task 5. Enter those into the [form]({{< var results-form-url >}}), and the mark appears without anything being fitted.
:::

## IDE quick fixes

| If ... | Then ... |
|---|---|
| A package will not load, or `try_spec` is "not found" | Run the checker again – `source("R/check_setup.R")` – and run the install line that it prints; or install by hand, for example `pak::pak("lme4")`. |
| The `pak` install that `R/check_setup.R` prints stalls or half-finishes | Restart R (Session menu), then run the install again; a second pass usually completes what the first left. |
| "Permission denied" while installing a package | Let R use a personal library that it can write to – accept the offer from R to create a personal library, then reinstall. |
| A data file is "not found" | Check that you opened the unzipped **folder** in your IDE (File → Open Folder in Positron and VS Code; the `.Rproj` file in RStudio), not a single file – the paths in the code are relative to that folder. |
| Task 3 says that the file could not be downloaded | Check the internet connection and run the chunk again. If the network of the venue blocks the OSF, carry on with Task 4: the rest of the report does not need the file. |
| lme4 warns that "some predictor variables are on very different scales" | Nothing to fix: GDP per head runs into tens of thousands while the attitudes run from 0 to 10, and the analyst met the same warning. |
| Something not listed here | The [setup help page](../../help.qmd) has the longer table, with prompts to give an AI assistant. |
| Everything is stuck | Open the [browser lab](lab.qmd) and carry on there. You lose nothing required. |

## Rendering the report {#rendering-the-report}

Render your report once your preregistration block is complete. The rendered copy carries the date on which it was rendered and keeps the declaration above the cells that fit the specification. In Positron and in RStudio, press the **Render** button at the top of the open report. In VS Code, run the Render command of the Quarto extension. In any of the three you can also run `quarto render index.qmd` in a terminal. On the browser lab page the same block is a cell on the page, and it updates in the tab when you run it.
